title: #herelieslove #herelieslovebway #herelieslovebroadway #herelieslovemu...
transcript: Last night, my sister and I saw Here Lies Love on Broadway, a musical about former First Lady of the Philippines, Imelda Marcos. It is genuinely one of the craziest shows I've ever seen. Theatre has been transformed into a nightclub with various types of seating or lack thereof. This, along with the disco like music, is meant to mimic karaoke, which has a long history in Filipino culture. It's hard to describe this experience because it's nothing like I've ever had in a Broadway theater before, but it is a feast for the senses. Production is extremely immersive and creative, and all the design elements work together to not only entertain but help guide the audience through the story. Was really impressed with the performances, particularly because I imagine it could be easy as a performer to be swallowed up by the surrounding production elements. But overall, the actors do a great job of commanding the story while interacting with audience members who are often meant to represent civilians. A lot of ways, this feels like a staged concert, and while I didn't love all of the music just to stand alone songs, I think it does a good job of conveying the story. David Byrne started this project over 10 years ago as a concept album, and it's wild to me how big it has become, how ambitious it is, and how so many choices do land really well. I would consider this one a must see with That another playbill from my collection
